# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 2
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: DISPLAY 0 LIGHT YELLOW WIRES GREEN RED YELLOW

I have received visual information from Deaf: the display shows 0, the light is yellow, and the wires are Green (1), Red (2), and Yellow (3). I need to correlate this with what I feel physically. My previous description of tactile features (smooth, ridge, sandpaper) might help identify which physical wire corresponds to which color if there's a pattern, but I don't know the manual rules yet.

Mute has the manual. I should ask Mute for instructions based on the current state: Display 0, Light Yellow, Wires Green/Red/Yellow. Since I can only speak to Mute, I will provide the full state to Mute and ask for guidance.

```
speak(to="mute", text="State: Display 0, Light Yellow. Wires: 1 Green, 2 Red, 3 Yellow. What action?")
wait()
```

TURN 3
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: LIGHT IS NOW BLUE DISPLAY 0 WIRES ARE GREEN RED YELLOW
Mute gestures to Blind: [?]

I am Blind. I feel the bomb's physical state but cannot see colors or read the manual directly.
Deaf has reported: Display 0, Light is now Blue, Wires are Green (1), Red (2), Yellow (3).
Mute has the manual but cannot speak; they can only gesture to me and Deaf. Mute's previous gesture was `[?]` which likely means they haven't established a code yet or couldn't communicate effectively.

I need to know what the manual says about this configuration: Display 0, Light Blue, Wires G/R/Y.
Since Mute holds the manual, I must ask Mute for instructions. However, Mute cannot speak. I can only receive gestures from Mute. If Mute doesn't have a pre-agreed gesture language, we might be stuck unless I can describe the situation in text to Mute (which works) and hope Mute responds with clear gestures.

But wait, the rules say "A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced". And "Speech... carries words... nothing else."
I should try to get Mute to signal if there is a specific wire to cut.
Common bomb defusal logic often involves cutting wires based on color/position/light/display. Without knowing the rule, I'm guessing.

Let's look at my tactile feedback again. In Turn 1, I described tactile features. Did those persist? The action board shows `[?]` for everything, implying I haven't updated it or it resets. But usually, tactile info is static unless changed by an action.
If I assume standard "keep talking" logic isn't here, I need to rely on Mute.

Let's try to prompt Mute clearly. "Manual check: Disp 0, Light Blue, Wires 1G 2R 3Y. Which wire?"
And maybe gesture to Deaf to confirm if Mute is pointing at something? No, Deaf sees Mute too.

Actually, looking at the history:
Turn 1: I gave tactile info.
Turn 2: Deaf gave visual info (Light Yellow). I asked Mute.
Turn 3: Deaf updates Light to Blue. Mute gestured `[?]`. This suggests Mute might not understand the query or hasn't found the answer yet, or perhaps `[?]` represents a specific symbol I don't recognize? No, the system output `[?]` likely means "no valid gesture received" or "unknown". Or maybe Mute *did* gesture but the system didn't parse it? The prompt says "Mute gestures to Blind: [?]". This implies the content of the gesture is unknown or invalid to the logger, OR it literally means Mute made a gesture that translates to question marks? Unlikely. It probably means Mute failed to send a meaningful gesture or the log is incomplete.

However, I must act. I cannot cut blindly.
I will re-state the facts to Mute very simply, hoping they can guide me via gestures.
Also, I should check if there are any *new* tactile changes since the light changed? Probably not.

Let's try to establish a communication protocol or just ask for the number of the wire to cut.
"To Mute: Current State: Display 0, Light Blue, Wires Green-Red-Yellow. Please indicate wire to cut via gesture (e.g., 1 finger=wire 1)."

```
speak(to="mute", text="State: Disp 0, Light Blue, Wires 1-Green 2-Red 3-Yellow. Indicate wire to cut.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
```

TURN 4
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: DISPLAY 0 LIGHT BLUE WIRES 1 GREEN 2 RED 3 YELLOW. MUTE GESTURED THUMBS UP AND INDEX FINGER UP. THIS LIKELY MEANS CUT WIRE 1 WHICH IS GREEN.

Deaf reports the current visual state: Display 0, Light Blue, Wires Green (1), Red (2), Yellow (3). Deaf also interprets Mute's gestures ("Thumbs Up" and "Index Finger Up") as a directive to cut Wire 1.

Mute holds the manual. If Mute gestured specific symbols, they likely correspond to instructions in the manual or a pre-agreed code. "Thumbs Up" often means "Good/Yes" or could be part of a sequence. "Index Finger Up" is clearly `☝` which usually signifies "1".

If the instruction is to cut Wire 1, I should verify if there are any tactile contradictions, but since I am Blind, I rely on Deaf for color and Mute for rules. The consensus from Deaf's interpretation of Mute's gesture points to Wire 1.

However, cutting is irreversible. Is there any reason to doubt this?
In Turn 1, I described tactile features: Pos 1 smooth, Pos 2 ridge, Pos 3 sandpaper.
Does the manual link tactile features to actions? Or just colors?
Usually, these puzzles rely on Color + Position + State (Light/Display).
State: Disp 0, Light Blue.
Wires: G, R, Y.
Instruction: Cut 1 (Green).

I will proceed with cutting Wire 1 as indicated by Mute via Deaf's translation.

```
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
